title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows (2026-04)
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview:

This reference consolidates Redwood Inference's mandatory controls and operational procedures for RBAC and authentication, audit logging and retention, data residency and deletion, secure SDLC gates, security incident response, compliance evidence collection, and risk/exception handling. It is intended for engineers, product owners, security, compliance, and customer-facing teams implementing or verifying controls.

Applicability:
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted services, the Dedicated control plane, and Redwood-managed artifacts for Private deployments.
- Third-party services must supply vendor attestations and be mapped to our control matrix; otherwise they are out of scope.

1) RBAC & Authentication
Purpose: Enforce least privilege and centralized authentication for humans and services.
Standards:
- Roles: owner, admin, dev, svc-account, auditor, support. Assign minimal privileges and scope resources by tag.
- SSO: All human access via Okta. MFA required for all human accounts.
- Service identities: Prefer short-lived tokens (OIDC/AWS STS) or workload identities. Long-lived keys require documented exception.
- Privileged access pattern: Just-in-time elevation with timebox, approval, and session recording for production actions.

RBAC Requirements (summary):
- owner | Platform/product owners | Org-wide | Quarterly
- admin | Infra & cluster admins | Project to org | Monthly
- dev | Engineers | Project | Quarterly
- svc-account | CI/CD, monitoring | Narrow resource scope, tag-based | Monthly
- auditor | Security/compliance reviewers | Read-only across systems | Quarterly

Onboarding/Offboarding Checklist:
1. Provision SSO account and assign role template.
2. Create scoped service identity and configure rotation.
3. Request JIT elevation for privileged tasks and record justification.
4. Offboard: disable SSO, rotate keys, remove role bindings, and run access review.

2) Audit Logging
Objectives: Maintain tamper-evident logs to support detection, investigation, and audit evidence.
Events to log:
- Authentication (SSO login, MFA events, JIT grants)
- Authorization changes (role bindings, policy edits)
- Admin actions (prod deploys, infra changes)
- Data access to sensitive stores (S3/KV/DB reads/writes)
- Security tool telemetry (scans, EDR alerts)

Retention & Integrity:
- Centralize logs in immutable (WORM) storage with checksums and index.
- Retention: security-critical 1095 days; operational 365 days; debug 90 days.
- Access: raw logs limited to security/audit roles; engineers receive extracts via ticketing.

Monitoring & Alerting:
- SIEM detections for brute force, privilege escalation, unusual data transfer, and retention modifications.
- High-severity findings auto-create incidents with SLA-driven owner assignment.

3) Data Residency & Retention
Principles:
- Store customer data only in contractual regions.
- Apply classification (Public, Internal, Confidential, Sensitive/PII) to determine controls and retention.
Controls:
- Region tags enforced by deployment pipelines and validated during deploy gates.
- Network egress controls and replication guards to prevent unauthorized cross-region copy.

Retention Matrix:
- Public | Model metadata | 12 months | n/a
- Internal | Metrics/telemetry | 12 months | preserved per legal hold
- Confidential | Customer configs | 7 years | preserved & access-limited
- Sensitive/PII | Customer content containing PII | contract-defined (default 7 years) | preserved until hold release

Deletion Process:
1. Owner sets lifecycle in config registry.
2. Automated lifecycle marks objects for soft-delete (30d).
3. Post soft-delete, objects are crypto-shredded (KMS rotate + irreversible delete).
4. Deletion validated by audit job and recorded in evidence store.

4) Secure SDLC
Goals: Shift security left and require evidence for audit controls.
Requirements:
- Threat models for new services or data flows involving sensitive material.
- SAST and dependency scans on every PR. Block merges on critical/high without mitigation.
- DAST/credentialed scans against staging pre-production.
- CI-integrated secrets detection; findings trigger rotation and incident creation.
- PR checklist: security reviewer, dependency review, infra-iam flagging, rollout plan.

Gating:
1. Automated checks (tests, lint, SAST) on PR.
2. Security review for auth/data changes.
3. Block merge until checks pass or exception approved.
4. Production deploy: canary rollout + security smoke tests.

5) Incident Response (Security)
Classification:
- Sev-P0: Active exfiltration or confirmed customer-data compromise.
- Sev-P1: Privilege escalation or service takeover risk.
- Sev-P2: Lateral movement or suspicious intrusion activity.
- Sev-P3: Low-impact security findings.

Playbook (summary):
1. Detect/Triage: SIEM/monitoring creates incident; on-call triages within 15 minutes.
2. Contain/Isolate: Network blocks, revoke sessions, suspend svc-accounts.
3. Preserve Evidence: Snapshot systems, collect immutable logs, preserve volatile memory if needed.
4. Remediate: Patch, rotate secrets/keys, harden configs.
5. Communicate: Follow notification timelines for impacted customers and regulators.
6. Postmortem: Publish within 14 days with timeline, impact, remediation, and action items.

Forensics & Legal:
- For P0/P1 incidents engage Legal and Customer Success immediately; preserve chain-of-custody and limit raw artifact distribution.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Purpose: Provide auditors with an auditable trail for controls (SOC2, ISO27001) and internal attestations.
Evidence types & storage:
- Policy docs and control mappings (versioned in compliance vault).
- System evidence (logs, config snapshots, access reviews) in WORM-backed evidence store.
- Human evidence (approvals, JIT requests, training records) exported from HR/Okta with metadata.

Collection Process:
1. Control owners tag artifacts in the evidence registry with control IDs.
2. Automated collectors ingest artifacts and store digests on schedule.
3. Manual evidence uploads include attestations and reviewer metadata.
4. Audit readiness: provide read-only snapshot for auditors and export mapping reports.

7) Risk & Exceptions
Process:
1. Submit exception with risk assessment, compensating controls, timeline, and owner.
2. Security scores and prescribes mitigation requirements.
3. Risk committee (security, engineering, legal, product) decides.
4. Approved exceptions are timeboxed (max 90 days) with remediation milestones and owner.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Implemented compensating controls (monitoring, segmentation).
- Defined remediation plan with milestones.
- Exception recorded in risk register and included in next audit snapshot.

8) Ownership & Escalation
Owners:
- Head of Security: Ethan Brooks
- Compliance Manager (evidence): Sofia Nguyen
- IAM Lead: Ravi Patel

Escalation:
- Critical incidents: Pager -> security on-call -> Security Manager -> CTO
- Risk exceptions: slack #sec-risk -> weekly risk committee

9) Appendix: Examples
IAM CLI snippet:
aws iam create-role --role-name redwood-service-role --assume-role-policy-document file://trust.json
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name redwood-service-role --policy-name scoped-access --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:GetObject"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-customer-data/*"]}]}'

Log retention YAML example:
retention:
  security_logs_days: 1095
  operational_logs_days: 365
  debug_logs_days: 90
